STEP 1 - Scene: A single plated meal of stir-fried noodles (looks like lo mein/chow mein style with beef or mushroom pieces, carrot, and cabbage) with a glass of pale yellow drink (lemonade or lemon-lime soda) and a paper cone of... (cup/cone cover visible). Photographed from a near-eye-level frontal angle on a tray, with a color calibration chart in the frame.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a white disposable round plate, roughly 20 cm diameter (side-plate size). Area = 3.14 x (10)^2 = 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) stir-fried noodles (wheat egg noodles), (b) sliced meat/mushroom pieces mixed in, (c) small amounts of carrot and cabbage/vegetables, (d) soy-based sauce glaze. Drink is separate and not counted.

STEP 4 - Area: Noodles cover ~75% of the plate area (the pile fills most of the plate interior, with some rim showing). Meat/mushroom pieces ~10%, vegetables ~5% (included in the noodle mass otherwise). Total covered ~80%, i.e., ~250 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: Noodle pile domed to ~2.5 cm average height. Noodles: 236 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 590 ml. Meat/mushroom pieces: 31 cm^2 x 1.0 cm ≈ 31 ml (sitting on top of noodles, partly overlapping, so counted in envelope). Vegetables: 16 cm^2 x 1.0 cm ≈ 16 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Noodles 590 ml x 0.8 ≈ 470 g (cooked, lightly oiled). Meat/mushroom 31 ml x 0.9 ≈ 28 g. Vegetables 16 ml x 0.6 ≈ 10 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Stir-fried noodles with oil and sauce ~150 kcal/100 g: 470 g → ~705 kcal. Beef/mushroom mix ~150 kcal/100 g: 28 g → ~42 kcal. Vegetables ~40 kcal/100 g: 10 g → ~4 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A fully covered ~20 cm plate of stir-fried noodles typically holds 300–450 g of cooked noodle dish; 480 g total is at the upper end but consistent with a dense, domed pile. Total ≈ 508 g, ~750 kcal. Plausible, though likely somewhat high; the noodle estimate is the main uncertainty.
